validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: CONFIRMED by >=2 independent sources. This is the well-documented Iran->Iraq gas export pipeline supplying Baghdad-area power plants, which began flowing in late June 2017. Al-Bayan Center (independent Iraqi think tank, Dec 2017) reports Iraq had imported 1.2 billion cubic meters via Iran's pipeline to Baghdad by end-2017 (~14 mcm/d); Columbia CGEP states 'Iran has been exporting pipeline gas to Iraq since mid-2017' with 7.8 bcm delivered in 2024; Washington Institute confirms peak-summer imports of ~70 mcm/d feeding Iraqi power plants. The sheet's own cited source (RFE/RL 2017, 'Iran Begins Pipeline Gas Exports To Iraq After Years Of Delay') is corroborated by all three. CLASSIFICATION: correct as gas / transmission. It is a cross-border gas transmission trunk, NOT an oil/NGL line -- it does not match any entry in the GulfPub Iraq oil roster, and GulfPub has no Iraq gas coverage. Do NOT confuse with the separate proposed 'Iran-Iraq-Syria pipeline' (Islamic/Friendship gas pipeline to the Mediterranean), which is a different project. DUPLICATE: no duplicate found in the 36-row Iraq gas operating roster -- this is the only Iran-origin cross-border line; the Baghdad-area internal distribution lines (e.g. Mahmudiyah-Besmaya) are separate assets not in this roster and carry different ProjectIDs. ATTRIBUTION: Fuel=Gas correct; End province Diyala is defensible (gas physically enters Iraq at the Naft Shahr/Mandali border in Diyala) though the actual delivery terminus is the Baghdad power-plant cluster (Sadr, Besmaya, Al-Quds, Mansuriya); Start='Iran' is correct but unnamed. STATUS caveat: CGEP notes exports were halted in late 2025 with uncertainty on resumption, and flows have repeatedly been suspended/resumed seasonally; the physical pipeline remains 'operating' but flow is intermittent -- worth a ResearcherNotes flag rather than a status change.

validity.researcher_notes: SPEC / UNITS CONCERN on Capacity. GEM records Capacity=35.00 with CapacityUnits='MMcf/d'. Every independent source quotes Iran->Iraq gas flows in million cubic METERS per day, never MMcf/d: Al-Bayan Center ~14 mcm/d (Dec 2017) and 'up to 25 million cubic meters to Baghdad daily' planned; Columbia CGEP 7.8 bcm in 2024 (~21 mcm/d avg); Washington Institute ~70 mcm/d peak summer (all Iran lines combined). 35 MMcf/d is only ~0.99 mcm/d -- roughly 35x too small and far below any reported flow, so the unit label is near-certainly wrong. The numeric '35' most plausibly originated as ~35 mcm/d (a widely cited contracted/target volume for the Baghdad line). I could not read the original RFE/RL text (403 to fetch) to pin the exact intended figure, so the value itself is flagged for review, not overwritten. LENGTH and DIAMETER remain blank; I could not corroborate either to the >=2-independent standard, so they are left UNRESOLVED rather than force-filled.

routes.corridor_desc: Cross-border gas transmission line: Iranian gas is delivered into Iraq at the eastern Diyala border (Naft Shahr/Mandali area) and runs WSW across Diyala province (through the Baqubah corridor) into the Baghdad power-plant cluster on the capital's eastern/southern outskirts (Sadr, Al-Quds, Mansuriya, and the Besmaya CCGT ~25 km east of Baghdad). Endpoints are established from independent sources naming Baghdad/Diyala as the destination and 2017 as start; the intermediate corridor is only loosely bounded. Coordinates are approximate, taken from the named places (Naft Shahr border area, Mandali, Baqubah, Baghdad, Besmaya), NOT from a surveyed pipeline centerline -- no pipeline geometry was fabricated. Loose bound => low route accuracy.
routes.researcher_notes: Endpoints (Iran origin -> Baghdad via Diyala) are corroborated by independent sources; sources confirm delivery to Baghdad-area power plants starting 2017. The exact Iranian injection point and the Iraqi-side pipe route are not published in verifiable detail, so I described the corridor in prose and gave named-place approximate coordinates rather than inventing a route. No coordinate was fabricated; where a precise point is unknown the location is described in words. Corridor bound is loose -> low accuracy suggested.

summary: P5855 Iran-Iraq Gas Pipeline: real, correctly classed gas transmission, no duplicate (confirmed, caveat); CONCERN=spec -- Capacity unit 'MMcf/d' is wrong (flows are in million cubic meters/day; 35 MMcf/d is ~35x too small); route corridor proposed Naft Shahr/Diyala border -> Baghdad power plants at low accuracy.
